corrections: panel a records 34 path primitives: the first extraction pass kept paths above y = 300 pt only and missed the two grey flight arrows of the bottom swarm's second row (y = 301-321 pt).
panel c's arrows are drawn as a shaft plus a 16.8 pt triangular head in page points, i.e. panel a's arrow style; matplotlib's "-|>" head is blunter and shorter at the same nominal size.
panel c's polar tick labels are placed at their reference page positions: matplotlib puts polar tick labels on the grid circle, which lands "±180°" on top of the 180° grid line.
panel b prints four ELPD ticks where the reference page prints three, because our axis spans to -3581.7 rather than -3549.6.

panel c is not the reference page's panel any more: the observed-data band is gone (that comparison is panel e's, where both models' predictive densities meet the data), the bimodal predictive density stays as faint context, and the two hypothesis densities of panel d are marked at their directions - optic flow at 0 degrees, vectorial encoding at both +/-90 - against the uniform reference, drawn as a dashed circle.  The markers are point estimates only: their +/-HDIs would be 3.6 pt long at the polar's scale (shorter than a marker), so panel d remains the place the intervals are read.  Its title is renamed from the reference page's "Population-level predictive check" to "Predictive density" accordingly; panel_a.json keeps the reference wording.

panel e repeats panel c's polar geometry exactly (r = 1.0 circle 118.7 pt, centre 206.3 pt below its row's top), which is why the third row is the reference's own row height of 345 pt: like panel c, the polar's tick labels need 261 pt of height, and the row title sits above them.  Its legend takes the reference legend's clearance of 142.9 pt above the polar circle, mirrored onto the page's left half.

panel f's axes is 216 pt tall against panel d's 97.9: the house swarm sets its y limits in points (4 * the stack reach + 4 * the packing clearance), and the axes height has to equal that number, or the packing the function computes is not the packing that gets drawn.  Dots are drawn 5.0 pt and packed 6.0 pt apart: packed at their own size they only touch, and the vectorial-encoding row, where all 52 animals fall within 1.2 ELPD, then reads as one solid block.
known_differences: The page is 900 x 945 pt against the reference's 900 x 600: panels e and f are a row added below the reference figure's four, not a redrawing of anything on its page, and they take letters, titles and row height (345 pt, the reference's tallest row) in the reference's own measures so panel e sits at panel c's size exactly.  Panels a, b and d are unchanged and still fill the reference's 900 x 600 (their text and drawing positions match the previous build; see "verification"); c is redrawn (see corrections).
Text is set in Arial; the reference page uses Helvetica Neue, whose glyph widths differ by 1-4% at the same size and position.
Panel b's cached unimodal fit gives ELPD -3533.40 +/- 38.34 where the reference page prints -3502.0 +/- 38.8; the bimodal fit matches (-3404.51 +/- 39.27 against -3403.8 +/- 39.2).

panels_a_b_d_against_the_previous_build.method: text spans and drawing primitives within the reference page's own 900 x 600 (panel c excluded), compared between the previously committed PDF and this one
panels_a_b_d_against_the_previous_build.drawing_primitives: 66 of 68 identical to 0.05 pt; the two that move are the page background rectangle (600 -> 945 pt) and one photo-layer fill, by 0.01 pt
panels_a_b_d_against_the_previous_build.png_note: over the same region the committed PNG does differ (mean |difference| 8.5 of 255 over 4.3% of pixels): matplotlib places every axes from the bottom of the page, so changing the page height re-lays the raster phase of the whole figure.  900 pt is exactly 3750 px at 300 dpi and 945 pt is 3937.5, and no taller page reproduces the old grid, so this one is not recoverable.

mean_abs_pixel_difference_against_refere.method: 300 dpi, over each panel's own page region, with the best shift within +/-4 px taken up; panel c is the one panel here drawn to a different brief than the reference's, so its number is not comparable.
